msContents.summary:
[p][b]Contents[/b][/p]
[p]1. ff. 1r-53v Rhazes, [i]Liber divisionum[/i][/p]
[p]Title: 'Incipiunt [diuisiones rasis]]'[/p]
[p]Incipit: 'U[entilata in presentia] cuiusdam [uiri probi rememo] ratio diuisionum...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...et medicine que eradicant pannum. Expliciunt diuisiones RASIS'.[/p]
[p]f. 54r-v blank[/p]
[p]2. ff. 55r-103v Constantine the African, [i]Viaticum[/i], incomplete[/p]
[p]Title: 'Quoniam quidem ut in rethoricis tullius testatum...'.[/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Capillus ex fumo grosso et calido...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '..ex grauitate et grossitudine descendit ad inferiora et findit manus etc.'[/p]
[p]3. ff. 104r-145v Gilbert the Englishman, Commentary on the [i]De urinis[/i] of Gilles de Corbeil[/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Sicut dicit constantinus in pantegni...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...residuum sermonis est intellectum. Expliciunt uersus egidii cum comento gilberti. deo gracias.'[/p]
[p]4. ff. 146r-166v Gentile da Foligno, Commentary on the [i]De urinis[/i] of Gilles de Corbeil, incomplete[/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Liber iste quem legendum proponimus liber est noue institutionis...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...potest fieri resolutio quia nulla resolutio ideo'.[/p]
[p]ff. 167r-168r blank.[/p]
[p]5. ff. 169r-183r Roger of Salerno, [i]Chirurgia parva[/i][/p]
[p]Title: 'Hic incipit parua Rogerina. Assit principio sancta Maria nostro'.[p]
[p]Incipit: 'Cum artis medicine due sint partes...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...nec in eo tempore in quo mulier solet habere menstrua. Explicit parua Rogerina'.[/p]
[p]6. ff. 184r-185v Glossary of herbs in Latin, French and English[/p]
[p]Begins: 'Appalim gallice pelle unde apella...'[/p]
[p]Ends: '...Valeriana frigida idem. Explicit herbarium. Explicit herbrarium'.[/p]
[p]7. ff. 185v-186r Anonymous, [i]Tabula electuariorum[/i][/p]
[p]Begins: 'Electuaria calefacientia sunt hec. Diamargariton...'[/p]
[p]Ends: '...Syrupus violaceus et oxisaccharum'.[/p]
[p]8. ff. 186r-191v John of St. Paul, [i]Flores dietarum[/i][/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Corpus hominis ex iiii humoribus constat...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...ex commestione allii et portulacis et casel'[/p]
[p]9. ff. 192r-215v Matthaeus Platearius, [i]Circa instans[/i][/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Circa instans negotium in simplicibus medicinis...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...non nocet uero propter diuternam decoctionem. Hic liber est scriptus qui scripsit sit benedictus. Explicit hoc torum pro christo da mihi potum.'[/p]
[p]On Matthaeus Platearius's [i]Circa instans[/i] see Frank J. Anderson, [i]An Illustrated History of the Herbals[/i] (New York: Columbia University Press, 1997), pp. 45-50; and Minta Collins, [i]Medieval Herbals: The Illustrative Traditions[/i] (London: The British Library, 2000), pp. 239, 243, 285-286, 298, 307-308.[/p]
[p]10. ff. 215v-216r Anonymous, [i]De urtica[/i], in verse[/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Arbitror urticam multum in orbe fore generatam...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: 'Et dessicatum multis erit utile causis'.[/p]
[p]11. ff. 216v-219r Pseudo-Hippocrates, [i]Epizonium[/i][/p]
[p]Incipit: '[E]pizonium ipocratis quod est manifestum ad obseruandum die salutis et mortis...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...in eadem finiuit [?] uita [?] ex eadem illa [?] frenentes [?] purgat'[/p]
[p]12. f. 219r Pseudo-Hippocrates, [i]Capsula eburnea[/i], incomplete[/p]
[p]Incipit: '[P]eruenit ad me quod cum ypocras morti appropinquaret...'[/p]
[p]Ends imperfectly: '...et significat quod principio egritudinis'[/p]
[p]ff. 220r-v blank[/p]
[p]13. ff. 221r-252r Anonymous, definitions of difficult Latin, Greek and Arabic medical terms[/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Aer idem quod dius. Arson idem quod ciclamen...'[/p]
[p]Explicit:'...Zuccoraria. N[omen?] in metridato. flos angni [sic] casti. Explicit Liber Iste.'[/p]
[p]14. ff. 252v-253r Nicholas Praepositus, [i]Quid pro quo[/i][/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Pro aristologia ruta domestica...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...pro yssopo. Thymum. Explicit quid pro quo.'[/p]
[p]15. ff. 253r-257v Arnold of Villanova, [i]De conferentibus et nocentibus[/i][/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Conferunt cerebro fetida...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...Omne iuuans ventosum. Explicit tractatus do conferentibus et nociuis.
[p]16. ff. 257v-258v Notes on medical weights and measures, receipts, etc.[/p]
[p]f. 259r-v blank.[/p]
[p]17. ff. 260r-263r, alphabetical list of herbs, with synonyms[/p]
[p]Begins: 'Amarusca. anglice maathe...'[/p]
[p]Ends: 'Christiana...et inde paruuli stipites exeuntes. Expliciunt nomina Herbarum.'[/p]
[p]18. ff. 263r-266r Trotula, [i]De ornatu mulierum[/i][/p]
[p]Monica Green has identified this as one of the texts which made up the "Trotula Ensemble", although it is not mentioned in her articles "A Handlist of the Latin and Vernacular Manuscripts of the So-Called Trotula Texts. Part I: The Latin Manuscripts" and "Part II: The Vernacular Texts and Latin Re-Writings", Scriptorium 50 (1996), pp 137-175, 51 (1997), pp 80-104 (email communication, 19 Jan 2009) [/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Ut mulier suauissima et planissima videatur...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...ad virum secure attendat etc. Hec de ornatu mulierum dicta sufficiant. Explicit Liber. De Ornatu. mulierum. Secundum Galienum.'[/p]
[p]19. ff. 266v-280v Lanfranc of Milan, [i]Chirurgia parva[/i][/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Intendens uenerabilis amiee bernarde....'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...succus malorum macianorum. 1. de bosto.'[p]
[p]20. ff. 280v-297r Rhazes, [i]De doloribus juncturarum[/i][/p]
[p]Incipit: 'Dixit rases uolo in hoc capitulo dicere medicins...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...accipe ceruse. 3 . 1. cuforbii. 3. 1. oleum quod sufficit. confice.'[/p]
[p]21. ff. 297r-307r Anonymous, [i]Experimenta[/i][p]
[p]Incipit: 'Dixit Galienus. Ignis qui descendit super altare...'[/p]
[p]Explicit: '...donec remaneat libra. 1. cola.'[/p]
[p]For a discussion of the 'Experimenta' of 'Galen' or Rasis, see Thorndike [i]A History of Magic and Experimental Science[/i] Vol. II pp. 751 et seq.[/p]

msItem.title: Compendium of learned medical treatises (Miscellanea Medica XXI)

objectDesc.supportDesc: 1 volume307 ll. 4to. 20 1/2 x 14 cm. On vellum: 18th century quarter calf binding over wooden boards: back-strip damaged. Nos. 2, 4, and the last work are incomplete. Ff. 62, 63, 72, 98 are slightly defective: the first and last leaves stained and rubbed. Between fol. 98 and fol. 99 is a contemporary inserted vellum slip. There are three main scripts, and two others.
